content:
Ibrahim Khan: heads up: snippet parity is drifting again across Python/TS/Go. docs snippets should *compile* and have same behavior (timeouts/retries/streaming). can we align today so writers can lock copy?

Wei Chen: +1. I’m seeing 3 different env var names in drafts (`REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_KEY`, `API_KEY`). also the TS streaming snippet uses a different method name than the SDK docs.

Dana Lo: yeah TS example in the docs PR is using `client.chat.completions.create({ stream: true })` but the SDK moved to `client.responses.stream(...)` last month.

Monica Patel: ok let’s settle the contract for onboarding snippets. checklist is going to deep link to these and we can’t keep changing call shapes.

Ibrahim Khan: proposal (baseline contract for phase 1):
- env var: `REDWOOD_API_KEY`
- base URL: default (no `baseURL` in snippets unless explicitly calling out region)
- request id: show how to set `X-Request-ID` (or sdk option) so support can correlate
- retries: SDK default is ok but snippet should show *where* to configure max retries/backoff
- timeout: explicit per-request timeout (30s?)
- streaming: show proper iteration + disconnect handling note

Wei Chen: can we please keep the snippet minimal? writers are trying to keep “first request” under ~25 lines.

Monica Patel: we can do two tiers:
1) “First request” minimal (auth + one call + print)
2) “Production-ish” snippet (timeouts/retries/request-id + streaming)
Checklist step can link to (2) but in quickstart we can keep (1) as the first page.

Dana Lo: on TS specifically: right now:
- retries are done via `maxRetries` on client
- timeout is `timeoutMs` (client-wide)
- request id is `headers: { 'X-Request-ID': ... }` per call
I can make a helper function used in docs.

Ibrahim Khan: python SDK is currently:
- retries: `max_retries` on client
- timeout: `timeout` on request or client (we recently changed defaults in pr-388)
- request id: `extra_headers={"X-Request-ID": ...}`
Go is different bc context timeouts.

Elliot Price: from docs side: the main pain is method names. when they change, snippets in 6 places break.

Monica Patel: can we commit to “stable surface” for onboarding pages? even if internally we deprecate, we keep the snippet API stable for at least a quarter.

Dana Lo: i can add an alias in TS SDK so both `responses.create` and `chat.completions.create` work, but it’s messy. better to pick one.

Ibrahim Khan: I vote we standardize on the newer “responses” style across all SDKs (matches product direction). but python + go need to confirm they expose it.

Monica Patel: python has `client.responses.create(...)` already right?

Ibrahim Khan: yep (behind the scenes it hits the same endpoint). go has `Responses.Create` (i think) but snippet in docs still uses `ChatCompletions`.

Wei Chen: if we standardize on “responses” nomenclature, we need to update the checklist copy too (“make your first response”). not a big deal but want to avoid confusing people used to “chat completions”.

Nadia Rahman: +1 on request-id. support + telemetry folks keep asking for a consistent header name. please don’t invent per-language names.

Ibrahim Khan: ok request-id header name: `X-Request-ID`. generated client-side. we can show `uuid4()` / `crypto.randomUUID()` / `uuid.NewString()`.

Dana Lo: TS snippet suggestion (prod-ish):
```ts
import { Redwood } from "@redwood-ai/sdk";

const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY!, maxRetries: 3, timeoutMs: 30_000 });

const requestId = crypto.randomUUID();
const stream = await client.responses.stream({
  model: "redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
  input: "Write a haiku about GPU batching.",
  headers: { "X-Request-ID": requestId },
});

for await (const event of stream) {
  if (event.type === "output_text.delta") process.stdout.write(event.delta);
}
```
Need to confirm event names are actually that :grimacing:

Ibrahim Khan: python is similar but event typing differs. also our python streaming yields `TextDelta` objects not raw event types.

Monica Patel: this is exactly the issue. the streaming loop should look consistent even if internal event type names differ.

Elliot Price: can we avoid event-type branching in the onboarding snippet and just show `for chunk in stream: print(chunk.text, end="")` style?

Ibrahim Khan: python can do:
```py
for event in stream:
    if event.type == "output_text.delta":
        print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)
```
But if TS/go don’t have the same `type` strings, it’s going to diverge.

Dana Lo: TS currently exposes `for await (const text of stream.text()) { ... }` helper, which avoids event types.

Monica Patel: that’s good. do python/go have a similar helper?

Ibrahim Khan: python has `stream.text_deltas()` (added last sprint). go has `TextDeltas()` iterator (I think). we should standardize those names if possible.

Wei Chen: from docs POV, “stream.text_deltas()” / “stream.textDeltas()” / “stream.TextDeltas()” is fine. the concept is the same and we avoid event tax.

Monica Patel: great. action items:
- SDK leads: ensure each SDK exposes a text-deltas helper for streaming and that snippet compiles.
- Writers: update onboarding pages to use text-deltas helper (no event-type switch).
- All: standardize env var + request-id header.

GitHub: PR opened by Ibrahim Khan: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-sdk-python/pull/388

Ibrahim Khan: pr-388 already improves retry/backoff defaults + adds `text_deltas()` to the stream object. i’ll make sure it’s in the released version referenced by docs.

Dana Lo: TS side: pr-512 adds streaming stability + already has `stream.textDeltas()` helper. i’ll double-check signature + docs snippet.

Elliot Price: can we also align error handling in snippets? right now TS catches `Error` and python catches `RedwoodError` with different fields.

Monica Patel: minimum: show how to log `request_id` and `status` and mention 401/429 quickly. we don’t need a giant taxonomy in onboarding snippet.

Nadia Rahman: careful: don’t log headers that could include api key. just log request-id + status + error code.

Ibrahim Khan: ok canonical error pattern:
- print `err.status_code` (or equivalent)
- print `err.code` / `err.type` if available
- print request-id if present in response headers OR the client-generated one (we have it already)

Wei Chen: +1. we’ll link to troubleshooting page for the rest.

Dana Lo: TS snippet for errors:
```ts
try {
  // call
} catch (err: any) {
  console.error("request failed", { requestId, status: err.status, code: err.code });
  throw err;
}
```

Ibrahim Khan: python:
```py
try:
    ...
except Exception as e:
    print("request failed", {"request_id": request_id})
    raise
```
But we should catch `RedwoodAPIError` specifically to access status/code.

Monica Patel: ok, Ibrahim please update python snippet guide to catch the typed error. Dana do same for TS. We’ll accept Go being a little verbose with `errors.As`.

Wei Chen: timeline check: i need final snippet shapes by EOD tomorrow to finish copy.

Monica Patel: locking decisions now:
1) Use `responses` API in all snippets.
2) Streaming uses text-deltas helper (no event types).
3) Env var = `REDWOOD_API_KEY`.
4) Explicit timeout and maxRetries in “production-ish” snippets.
5) Always set `X-Request-ID` header; show how to generate.
If any SDK can’t support this by tomorrow, we’ll adjust the snippet set to match the lowest common denominator.

Ibrahim Khan: confirmed python can do all 5.

Dana Lo: confirmed TS can do all 5.

Elliot Price: pinging Go owner separately but I think it’s doable. thanks all.

Monica Patel: cool. Wei/Elliot: once you update docs, please drop links here so we can run a quick “snippets compile” check across repos.

Wei Chen: will do. also please don’t rename `text_deltas()` between now and GA :)

Ibrahim Khan: lol. we’ll treat it as part of onboarding contract. :thumbsup:

Dana Lo: :thumbsup: i’ll add a tiny snippet test in TS docs build to catch drift.

Monica Patel: +1 let’s add snippet tests across sdk repos. follow-up ticket after we get beta out.
